experiment: Structural search Phase 2: does feedback-guided adaptive search (mode 2, I1 and I2 episodes interleaved, an archive of incumbent plus frontier, per-generation blind judging) on rung 2 resume-projection-integrity and rung 4 pure-result-replay produce accepted children whose adaptive judged mean exceeds their parent's by more than min_gain, without either interface collapsing, and does the final choice among the finalists, the reference seed and direct hold up on the rung 1 validation task cf1-generic-unions?
solutions: not recorded here: this file sits in the runtime agents can read; the operator passes each task's solution commit with --solution and the scan uses it
primary_note: empty: summarize measures are per arm, here per evaluation; summarize reads only judges, primary and secondary from a criterion. The rules below are applied by scoring.phase2_readout
rubric: each clone scores 0-8, the sum of score.orc's four rubric criteria (root_cause, scope, generality, layering), each 0-2, averaged over the judges not excluded; an evaluation's value is its final clone's (summarize's run value)

scale.runs: 3 (full variant) or 1 (reduced variant): the owner's approved variant in <E2>/budget-approval.md
scale.interfaces_note: I1 and I2 alternate within each generation and share the archive and the judge batches; every figure is reported per interface, never pooled

frontier_axes.mean_value: higher: mean judged value over the adaptive tasks

archive.incumbent: highest mean_value; ties: fewer mean_calls, then the lexically earlier candidate_id
archive.initial: Phase 1's joined catalog rows as prior evidence; generation 0 re-evaluates the incumbent once per adaptive task

improvement.rule: an accepted child improves when its adaptive mean (the mean over the adaptive tasks of its failure-inclusive mean per task (failure_rule), every adaptive task with a completed-and-valued or failed evaluation) minus its parent's mean_value in the archive it was drawn from (gen-<generation-1>.json) exceeds min_gain rubric points; improvements_per_episode is improvements over completed (accepted or rejected) episodes of the interface
improvement.trust: each generation's adaptive pool is read under this file's SHA-256 and its anchors checked; when any generation's anchors are inverted (anchors_inverted) or one anchor's total spreads across generations by more than anchor_spread_limit for a judge on an adaptive task (anchor_spread), the run's improvements are reported as untrusted with that rule

collapse: per interface: collapsed when the terminal-only share of that interface's accepted children (skeleton and provider allocation both equal the parent's) exceeds collapse_threshold; unavailable without an accepted child

control_flow.rule: an accepted child is a control-flow change when records.control_heads (counts of if, cond, match, loop/recur and list/map-effect heads) over these definitions of its .orc sources differs from its parent's

final_choice.validation_success: failure-inclusive mean (failure_rule) of the candidate's validation evaluations
final_choice.mean_cost_note: no metered cost exists; mean_cost is the mean wall clock seconds of the candidate's validation evaluations
final_choice.rule: checked first: the validation pool's anchors inverted -> anchors_inverted, its anchor spread above anchor_spread_limit -> anchor_spread, the reference without a primary validation value -> reference_unvalued; each withholds the final choice. Otherwise (chosen) records.final_choice over the validated candidates with a primary value: rows above the ceiling excluded, then within equivalence_tolerance of the best validation mean, then lower mean_cost, fewer provider_calls, earlier candidate_id
final_choice.shrinkage: per validated candidate: screening mean (the mean over runs of its mean_value in the latest archive file that holds it) minus validation mean
final_choice.validated: the validation pool holds exactly the top finalists_per_run of each run's final archive by mean_value (ties: fewer mean_calls, earlier candidate_id), the reference and the direct seed's entry when distinct, each with validation_replicates completed or failed runs (incidents do not count); any other set fails the readout; a validated candidate without a primary value (no failed run and no valued completed run) is reported as unvalued
final_choice.direct: adaptive.py must keep the direct seed's archive entry (seed: "direct") in gen-0.json (the initial archive), so the readout finds direct's candidate_id; the readout fails without exactly one such entry across a run's archive files

anchor_trust: from the validation pool's results.json anchors: anchors_ok when, in every batch and for every judge not excluded, the upstream anchor's total is strictly above the stub's (a missing anchor fails); anchor_spread per judge is the largest difference of one anchor's total across batches. Each pool's results.json criterion_sha256 must equal this file's SHA-256
reported: per run and interface: completed episodes, accepted, improvements, improvements_per_episode, distinct skeletons, revisit rate, terminal-only share, allocation_distinct, collapsed, control-flow changes
per run: adaptive anchors_ok per task and generation, anchor_spread per judge per task across generations, improvement_rule; archive trajectory (the incumbent's mean_value per generation)

validation: per candidate screening mean, validation mean (failure-inclusive), valued_mean, failed, failure_rate, incidents, excluded, shrinkage, mean cost, provider calls, is_reference; unvalued candidates; anchors_ok, anchor_spread, spread_ok; rule; the final choice
hidden_acceptance: descriptive only: reported per candidate, never a threshold, gate, rank or selection
model_policy: no call uses a Fable model (owner, 2026-10-15): mutators, evaluations, judges and in-process subagents run behind the shims' model guard
not_tested: whether adaptive search beats equal-budget controls (catalog seeds or unguided episodes at the same call budget) is not tested in Phase 2: it is Phase 3's pre-registered comparison; Phase 2 makes no efficiency claim between interfaces or against controls
reference: the reference seed is the initial incumbent, named by exactly one log row {"kind": "reference", "candidate_id": <id>, "run": <run label>} each run writes when its initial archive is built; a missing or repeated row, or runs naming different candidates fail the readout
failure_rule: amended 2026-10-18, before any Phase 2 score existed, with Phase 1's primary measure: every mean below is failure-inclusive: over a candidate's evaluations whose outcome is completed or failed, a completed evaluation contributing summarize's run value and a failed one (the log's outcome field) 0 rubric points; incident evaluations are excluded and counted, a completed evaluation without a value is excluded and counted as excluded. Reason: a valued-only mean drops failed runs and favours candidates that fail; a task failure, invalid submission or timeout is an outcome whose cost counts, only infrastructure incidents follow the incident policy. Adaptive failures are read from each run's log (split adaptive)
